summary: Togo waives visas for ECOWAS citizens and, for stays of up to 30 days, for all other African nationals, and its Visa Assistant also answers 'no visa needed' for Malaysian and Singaporean passports. Everyone else needs an eVisa applied for on voyage.gouv.tg at least 5 days before arrival (Togo Voyage recommends six working days) — visas on arrival are suspended. Every traveller entering Togo by air also completes the portal's online immigration form before arrival.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Togo?
faq.answer: Citizens of ECOWAS countries enter visa-free, and all other African nationals may stay up to 30 days without a visa. Togo's Visa Assistant also answers that Malaysian and Singaporean passports need no visa. Everyone else needs the official eVisa from voyage.gouv.tg, applied for at least 5 days before arrival (Togo Voyage recommends six working days): visas on arrival are suspended. All travellers arriving by air must complete the online immigration form before arrival.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Togo?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Togo.

faq.question: Is Togo safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK government advises against all travel within 5 km of the Burkina Faso border and against all but essential travel to the rest of the far-northern Savanes region, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Togo. It also says violent crime, theft and pickpocketing are common, particularly on the beaches and in the markets of Lomé.

faq.question: Can I enter Togo overland from Ghana or Benin?
faq.answer: Yes. ECOWAS citizens need no visa, though Togo Voyage tells them to complete their immigration formalities online on voyage.gouv.tg before reaching the border. Other nationalities who need a visa must arrive with an approved eVisa, since visas on arrival are suspended.
